title: Interaction between ventilation strategy, lung volume, and hemodynamics in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome
summary:
The use of positive pressure ventilation in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) leads to an uneven ventilation distribution in the lungs. The consequences of this uneven distribution are the collapse of poorly ventilated lung areas (atelectasis) and the overdistension of well ventilated lung areas (hyperinflation). These changes increase the risk of ventilation-induced lung injury during therapy. 

One way to improve the ventilation distribution in the lungs is to use positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP). The positive pressure in the lungs at the end of exhalation counteracts the pressures acting on the lungs from outside; the difference is called "transpulmonary pressure". When transpulmonary pressure is positive, collapse of the lung regions is prevented.

A certain transpulmonary pressure can be achieved by adjusting the pressure during exhalation (PEEP).  This influences the volume of respiratory gas in the lungs. At the same time, there is also an interaction between respiratory gas volume in the lungs and cardiovascular function.
The aim of the study is to investigate the effects of different ventilation settings with regard to their effects on respiratory gas volume in the lungs and cardiovascular function. The objective is to identify the optimal individual setting that achieves a favorable distribution of respiratory gases in the lungs while preserving cardiovascular function.

interventions.name:
To investigate the influence of individualized settings of tidal volume and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) on pulmonary ventilation distribution, lung mechanics and volume, gas exchange and hemodynamics.
The sequence of individualized tidal volume and PEEP settings is randomized.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Moderate to severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with PaO2/FiO2 ≤150 mmHg
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years, contraindications to prone positioning, pregnancy, presence of a cardiac pacemaker and/or implanted defibrillator, and life expectancy < 24 hours.
